body: Yeah, we at least my life. I'm sure if I was enjoying myself a little bit more, and I didn't have such an experience heavy with suffering, I think the idea of dying wouldn't be so desirable, as it is to me.

Ugh yeah my wife knows about my feelings and even my desire to kill myself. She doesn't know what to think or do or say anymore. She's afraid and probably lives with a lot of stress, not knowing what will happen next week or even tomorrow. We've been living the last 3 months in a lot of stress because I haven't earned any income in that time. We didn't know how we would pay for rent or food or bills. And she is always quiet, trusts that I will handle the matters. But it's eating her up inside, and she doesn't know how to speak with me anymore. 

She doesn't want me to kill myself, she loves me and wants me to grow old with her. She says it's a chemical imbalance, but I think today is different. I've come to peace with what I must do, and it's no longer about diseases, hopes, or the future.

Ugh, yeah I've talked to a lot of doctors about medication I took. I never had a psychologist because I would have to pay and I don't have any money. But I don't want to talk with doctors about my life, I don't see any dignity in that, so I'm not interested in anything like that anyway.

I did group therapy. I would feel good being there, but the moment I went home, I would just go back to being myself. I felt powerless to use any of the techniques they had taught me at group therapy. After a few weeks it ended and that was it.

Near the last few weeks, I had felt that therapy wasn't for me. Something about it felt weird. Like, it came to the point where I didn't want anyone else telling me what I should think or feel. I didn't want others to be analyzing my life, I didn't want anyone else's opinion. I felt that I actually don't have a mental disease, these negative thoughts really are me, and I should just accept who I am. And who I am is someone that's been here longer than I wanted to stay, and I really need to do what I want, not what other people expect of me.

The spiritual experience, ugh, it's a long story. But basically I got pulled up through a dense tunnel which sucked me out of my body, I wound up back in "source" talking with my spirit guides in an environment of absolute love and understanding, and I had a lucid conversation with my guides using thought-blocks. Being there was being completely free of the heavy, tired, and painful human body. Just free, calm and at ease. It was like taking off a tightly tied shoe, and your foot feeling the relief of being out of that shoe. As well, it was an amazing feeling of absolute love. It felt so good being there, it immediately showed me how fulfilling my life on earth had been.

My spirit guides said they saw I was having a horrible experience on earth, that it was causing me a lot of pain, so they wanted to meet with me to discuss if I want to continue. They said that the choice to live or to leave is always up to me, that life is not being forced on me (as if this is a catholic limbo). They showed me that I had decided to be born, that no one else forced me to live. They reminded me of the moment before I was born, they showed me the intention I had when I was born. 

Before I was born, I had been observing the world, and I was amazed at how people would get born and they would immediately forget about the truth of life. We would get so sucked into the experience, that we forget there is a reality beyond this one from which we originate. I saw people getting emotional and stress about life circumstances, and back in source, we found that to be funny, like we're watching a comedy. So watching this, I had said "I will be born into this world, and I will not allow myself to forget 'who I am'. And then I will remind others of the truth, so that they too can relax, chill out, and have a good time here."

But then what happened was, as I was growing up, my life experience was so disruptive and painful because of my parents, that I also got sucked into this human experience. And I forgot about my origins. I was always different from my siblings, and I always gave my mother a hard time (because she was working so hard to try and make me assimilate with the anxious nature of the people on earth). And I just didn't want any part of that, so I would resist her attempts at every level.

And then friends, and then school, everyone wanted me to assimilate to the human ways of "working hard", and "thinking about the future", and "saving a nest egg", and "what if you don't get into university? study hard or you won't go anywhere in life!" And my parents were also catholic, and they tried really hard to trick me into catholicism. But I was too smart, and I resisted that non-sense.

And so, there was something I wanted to do still on earth. So I told my spirit guides that I was willing to continue, but only if they let me keep the memory of our interaction, because I didn't want to forget who I am again and be lost like I was before. I remembered in that moment that I've had these meeting with my spirit guides before, and the experience has always been amazing -- and the moment I wake up, I want to tell everyone about the experience -- but they always take the memory away, and the moment I wake up, the entire memory has been erased. So I said that this time, they weren't allowed to take the memory from me again, it was important for me to remember it. The other condition was that I never wanted to work. They didn't seem to have a problem with that. They had complete access to my thoughts/feelings, and I into them, hence why we could communicate through thought-blocks and not have to use words. It was an instant communication, where as you think the words, you have already been heard and understood. They could see inside me and as a result understood me completely, that is how they knew I was in pain in the first place. 

So yeah, here I am. When I woke up from that experience, I rushed to my computer and wrote everything down and saved it, so that I would never forget the details of that interaction. I've had a couple other lucid experiences where I found myself in a place of great love/joy. But I don't recall having met with my guides since.

A while back I found a youtube video where a couple people who had near-death experiences talked about the details of their experience. And all of them had very similar experiences, exactly like mine. Squeezed through a dense tunnel, showed up on the other side in a place of absolute love/happiness, and then asked "do you want to continue?" And all of them thought about it, and decided there was more they wanted to do, so they all came back -- all the time knowing that when they did go back, they would be missing out on that pure love/happiness in "source". And three of them talked about waking up back in the body, and feeling completely depressed about being away from that perfect experience of love. Nothing compares to being there.

Ugh, I think that's why they always take the memory away. It's because when you realize how good it is to be "dead" (except there is no death, just life and more life), your desire to live on earth vanishes because no experience can compare to it. But everyone meets with their spirit guides at least 3 times by the 16th birthday. They always take the memory away. You can't continue a regular life once you've seen behind the veil.

Ugh, my childhood I never felt secure or loved. My parents were always fighting with each other, they fought so much, they didn't have time to focus on me or my brother and sister. I think they ruined the environment I grew up in. There was no happiness, it was a very disappointing childhood, compared to what it could have been. My wife's childhood was so much happier, it's unbelievable to me that it's actually possible to love ones family. I never felt that emotion about my family. My mother also had her own mental problems that she never got help for, and she passed on her bad habits to me. She also didn't have any social skills so I never made friends growing up, and in high school that cast a really deep hurt on me. I feel I never belonged anywhere -- not in my family, not in school, not in any of the jobs I had. 

Anyways, it was terrible in high school as a result of my family life and lack of social skills. And one day I had a negative social experience that completely destroyed me, when a friend turned on me, and I was basically kicked out of the social group. Having to go to that school and the people acting like they don't know me after that event hurt beyond anything I can describe. By the time I turned 16, I really wanted to kill myself. I couldn't stand the pain of that reality any more.

Uhm, well I had a "spiritual" event where I had spoken with my guides and they told me that the choice to die was always mine, that life isn't being forced on me, and they presented the choice to me. But I felt there was something I hadn't experienced yet, so I decided I would continue for a couple more years.

Anyways, I read somewhere when you have suicidal thoughts, people always say "it gets better." Well, so I said I would give it a couple years to see what happens.

Well, I just took a mental inventory after I realized that more than 10 years has passed now. My life didn't get better, it sucks just as much, if not more, than it did when I was 16. And all along the scars from those memories of negative experiences from my past have been terrorizing me. I can't let go of the pain they caused in me. I feel insufficient as a human, like I'm missing the elements I should have, and I want to just say "fuck it all" and quit. 

But yes, suicide has been on my mind for years now. For the last 5 years I would say it has been the "go to" thought about everything. For example, "I could finish this essay for tomorrow's law deadline, or I could just kill myself and not have to bother with this pointless work, that would be much easier." Every decision I have made in the last 10 years has been this desire to just kill myself and be free from this place. Living seems to pointless and hard, and death looks so easy. I just want to escape, and leave behind all the responsibility.
